bull.b: Low leverage and positive equity give TuHURA a comparatively flexible capital structure while it advances development. This can reduce near-term balance-sheet pressure and preserve capacity to direct resources toward clinical programs, although it does not remove funding needs.

Access to a revolving facility maturing in 2031 provides a financing channel for operating needs over the medium term. That longer-dated liquidity can support continuity of research and corporate activities as the company progresses its development plans.

Targeting cancer therapies that address resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors and enhance anti-tumor responses gives the development program a defined scientific focus. If clinical work succeeds, this focus could support differentiated treatment opportunities in oncology.

bear.b: Zero revenue across all reported periods confirms the company remains pre-commercial and has not established a product revenue base. Until candidates reach commercialization, operating funding must come from capital sources rather than recurring customer receipts, increasing execution dependence.

Net loss widened to about $30.6M TTM from $21.7M in 2024 and $8.3M in 2023, showing a rising cost burden before commercial revenue. Persistent losses can consume equity and constrain resources available for clinical development unless operating performance improves.

Operating cash flow deteriorated to about negative $29.7M TTM from negative $27.6M in 2025 and negative $14.7M in 2024; free cash flow was negative $29.9M. This burn makes ongoing external financing central to sustaining operations.
